I’ll inspect the PR’s description, diff, and checks, then trace the changed code in the local repository so I can explain both the behavior and the tradeoffs.

The change is narrowly targeted: it replaces one lookup against a command’s top-level arguments with the parser’s existing “active arguments” abstraction. I’m checking that this abstraction is correct for every command shape, especially explicit clauses and `--` handling, rather than relying only on the new happy-path test.

Yes—this is a good, low-risk bug fix, and I’d merge it.

`parse_partial()` tracks the next positional argument using `active_args()`, which returns:

- normal command arguments for ordinary commands;
- clause arguments for commands with a clause.

But when parsing stopped, `record_stop()` incorrectly looked up that position only in `cmd.args`. Clause commands are forbidden from having top-level arguments, so that list is empty. Consequently, a bare clause command reported no next argument, and completions couldn’t offer that clause argument’s choices or custom completer.

The PR changes:

```rust
out.cmd.args.get(...)
```

to:

```rust
active_args(&out.cmd).get(...)
```

That makes the final lookup consistent with the rest of the parser. The new regression test verifies that a bare command with an implicit `<tool@version>` clause reports that argument as next. See the [one-file diff](https://github.com/jdx/usage/pull/1372/files) and [regression test](https://github.com/jdx/usage/blob/ec01ee4e4d5c0991eacb4cc86b6cd2f35227900b/lib/src/parse.rs#L6558-L6575).

Why I like it:

- It fixes the problem at the abstraction boundary where it originated.
- It preserves ordinary-command behavior because `active_args()` falls back to `cmd.args`.
- It should also correctly handle explicit clauses, not just implicit ones.
- CI, Windows, MSRV, security, and automated review checks all pass.

The only optional improvement would be an end-to-end completion test proving that choices or a custom completer actually appear. The parser regression already covers the faulty state, though, so I wouldn’t block merging on that. [PR #1372](https://github.com/jdx/usage/pull/1372) looks ready.
